$comment: Per-browser command-line flag overrides for GPU/compositing fixes.
Source of truth for browsers-gpu.nix — patches nixpkgs's wrapper
script to inject these flags before '"$@"' so every launch has them.
Backend evidence (Brave 1.89 + Chromium 147 + Mesa 24.2 + Iris Xe):
Native Wayland on KWin → 'Compositing: Software only' + 'Failed
to find drm render node path' (KWin doesn't deliver render node
accelerated', WebGPU works, but Tiger Lake VAAPI hardware video
decode triggers PIPELINE_ERROR_DECODE on H.264 mp4
decode (~5% CPU, no problem on i5-1135G7), GPU still composites
Backend resulting from these flags: ANGLE-OpenGL (NOT Vulkan).
Vulkan ANGLE backend is upstream-incompatible with --ozone-platform=x11.
For Vulkan WebGPU, use Firefox (different rendering pipeline).
browsers.<binname>.flags     extra args injected before "$@" in wrapper
browsers.<binname>.rationale why this flag set is needed (for grep)

brave.rationale: KDE Plasma 6 / KWin Wayland render-node bug + Tiger Lake VAAPI decode bug. See $comment block above.

google-chrome-stable.rationale: Same Chromium-on-KWin-Wayland bug; same Tiger Lake VAAPI bug.

vivaldi.rationale: Same Chromium-on-KWin-Wayland bug; same Tiger Lake VAAPI bug.

$exclude_comment: DO NOT add `chromium` here. The chromium nixpkgs package exposes
a `.override` attribute that downstream packages (electron, signal-
desktop, etc.) depend on for build-time recompilation. overrideAttrs
preserves .override, so this design IS now safe for chromium too —
but verify electron/signal still build before adding.
